title.en: Read the determinant as signed volume and collapse

summary: Show the determinant as the signed volume scaling, including the orientation flip at negative values and the collapse at zero.
objective: Make the determinant visible as a geometric consequence rather than as a computed number beside a shape.
applies_when: A transformation is applied to a volume, a parallelepiped or a set of three vectors.
The determinant, invertibility or orientation is displayed or discussed.
The user can drive the matrix towards a singular configuration.
example_prompts: Show the determinant as the volume of the transformed cube, including the flip.
Let me drive the matrix to singular and see what happens.
negative_signals: Scenes that only need a scalar readout with no geometric claim.
Numerical linear algebra topics such as conditioning, which need a different treatment.
not_for: Scenes that only need a scalar readout with no geometric claim.
Numerical linear algebra topics such as conditioning, which need a different treatment.

principles: The volume of a parallelepiped spanned by three vectors is the absolute value of their triple scalar product, so the determinant of the matrix of those vectors is a signed volume rather than an arbitrary number.
A zero triple product means the three vectors lie in a common plane, so the volume is zero and the transformation has collapsed a dimension; that is the geometric meaning of singularity.
The sign carries orientation. Because the cross product is anticommutative, swapping two vectors negates the determinant, and a negative determinant means the transformation reverses handedness.
The singular case is a legitimate linear map and should be reachable and inspectable, even though the inverse does not exist.
implementation: Draw the transformed unit volume and report the determinant beside it, computed from the same matrix.
Encode the sign visually, for example by a handedness indicator or a colour change at the flip, rather than only by a minus sign in the readout.
Let the parameters reach the singular configuration exactly and show the flattened image with an explicit label instead of a near-zero jitter.
Where an inverse is offered, disable it in the singular case with an explanation rather than producing large or arbitrary numbers.
Show the plane or line that the collapsed image occupies, since that is the informative part of a singular map.
observable_checks: Compare the reported determinant against the volume drawn for several matrices, including a negative one.
Swap two columns and confirm the sign changes and the handedness indicator flips.
Drive the matrix to singular and confirm the image is genuinely flat and labelled, and that any inverse control is disabled.
Scale one column by a factor and confirm the determinant scales by the same factor.

creative_affordances: The visual language for orientation reversal is open: mirrored labels, a handed glyph or a colour convention all work.
A staged animation that pauses at the collapse is often the clearest presentation.
known_limits: Authored interpretation guidance citing the triple product and coplanarity statements; it does not treat determinants in dimensions other than three geometrically.
Numerical detection of singularity depends on a tolerance that this rule does not fix.

claims.statement: The volume of a parallelepiped with adjacent edges given by three vectors is the absolute value of their triple scalar product, a zero triple scalar product means the three vectors lie in the same plane, and the cross product is anticommutative so that exchanging two vectors reverses the sign.
claims.scope: Three-dimensional vector geometry; it does not treat determinants of larger matrices or numerical conditioning.
